Name the two main cropping seasons of India with one crop each.
questions.a: Kharif (sown in June, harvested in September - paddy, maize, cotton) and Rabi (sown in October, harvested in March - wheat, gram, mustard).

questions.q: What decides whether a crop is kharif or rabi?
questions.a: The season in which it grows - kharif crops need the rainy season, rabi crops the cool winter.

questions.q: Why do farmers rotate crops between seasons?
questions.a: Different seasons suit different crops; rotation also keeps soil fertile and breaks pest cycles.
